recipes.name: Green Chile Spinach Quiche
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package shredded Colby-Monterey Jack cheese
1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and drained

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a small bowl; set aside.

Beat eggs in a mixing bowl until smooth. Whisk in flour mixture until no lumps remain. Stir in the Colby-Monterey Jack cheese, cottage cheese, spinach, green chiles, and melted butter until evenly blended. Divide mixture between pie crusts.

Bake quiches in the preheated oven for 15 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Continue baking until quiches are lightly browned, and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean, 35 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Green Chile Spinach Quiche
raw_recipe.description: This green chile quiche is one of a kind. My whole family loves this quiche, made with a fresh assortment of cheeses, spinach, and, of course, eggs.

review.reviewBody: I have made several great quiche's from allrecipes and this is by far the favorite. I have breakfast each Sun. a.m. with my adult children and their friends, and I followed this recipe exactly, except I used fresh spinach and sauteed' it with a tad of sweet onion. This recipe is much lighter having less cheese then the others I've made. My husband even said, "D, this was a great breakfast"! now I was happy to get that compliment. Also, I made homemade hashbrowns to go with it. Great success. Thanks.

This is my go-to quiche now. I added 1/2 pound of browned sausage and used cheddar cheese. The green chiles really make this recipe great, especially with the spicy sausage. I have also added asparagus cut on a 1" diagonal and pre-cooked til bite tender before adding it to the egg mixture. I have made it successfully in my convection oven: 375 degrees for 15 minutes, then 325 degrees for 30 minutes. The conventional oven works just as well. I recommend using a baking sheet under the foil pan to make transferring easy. The crust turns out great! Always get rave reviews!

I love this recipe and it’s been a favorite except for one thing. I make it without a crust and cleanup has been awful because so much sticks to my Pyrex pie pan. Well I think I found a better way. This time I went old school and coated the pan with butter then sprinkled with flour over the butter. Much less stick!! Hope this helps! Before I was just using butter or oil. The flour made the difference
Sautéed mushrooms, onions and 1 Lb. fresh spinach until dry. Substituted hatch chiles instead of green chiles. Added an additional 8OZ. Gruyere cheese. Best quiche ever.

I needed a recipe to help me use up some cottage cheese. I made it without a crust and baked it in a muffin tin to make individual portions (about 25 minutes at 350 degrees). I halved the recipe, and this gave me about 18 muffins. 

I omitted the spinach and used one four ounce can of diced roasted chile peppers as well as three fresh Anaheim peppers, deseeded and diced. I sauteed chopped onion and mushrooms in butter, followed by the fresh pepper. I added this mixture to the batter. I also used a combination of sharp cheddar and pepper jack cheeses for more flavor. Some garlic powder - although minced garlic might have been better. Didn't miss the spinach or the crust. I would probably make this again.
Great recipe! I added 1/2 cup cubed ham and used 3/4 cup of plain Greek yogurt - also makes great individual quiches in muffin tins (using paper muffin cups or phyllo dough.)

I reduced the recipe by a third so it would fit in one big pie dish. I did use 2 cans of chili though. I used the cheese that I had - Dubliner and Feta (I bet any kind of cheese is good) plus I sautéd fresh spinach with some onion and added chopped turkey sausage. It was super delicious!

Since there are only 2 of us , I just made half the recipe with a few ingredient alterations:
1. Added cheddar cheese to the colby-jack
2. Substituted ricotta for the cottage cheese
3. Substituted fresh chard for the spinach
4. Added 3 oz of chopped canadian bacon

Reduced the 350 degree cooking time to 3o minutes since there was only 1 quiche to be cooked.

The results were exceptional even with the changes. Will keep this recipe for a group breakfeast or brunch. It could very well become one of my favorites.

This was awesome as is. I did add additional spinach only because I love it. Next time, will try adding mushrooms, red bell pepper, and a Serrano chile ( all lightly sauteed prior to adding )
But was SO good. Make sure you make the 2, I gave one to a friend ( who loved it ), but would be good to freeze one also
Looking forward to trying this crustless also
Thank you !!!
Delicious! I used about 5 fresh green chilies instead of the canned ones, removing the core and seeds. I also sautéed fresh spinach instead of frozen. The taste is great!

No need to look any further! This is an easy quiche to make. The first time I made it I followed the recipe exactly-- and it was perfectly delicious! The second time, I halved the recipe for one pie and I used fresh spinach, which I sauteed with the butter called for and added in some diced mushrooms and ham-- it was fantastic. [Note: With the added ingredients there was a little extra mixture that didn't fit in the pie shell. So, I put it into small souffle cups and baked them along side the quiche for approx. 30min, removed them and finished cooking the quiche.] nom nom nom
Made this for a baby shower and everyone loved them! Definitely a keeper recipe!

Excellent quiche! I didn’t have canned roasted chilies however I did have fresh, so I roasted my own. I made one with a crust and the other crustless. I prefer my quiche with a crust and still thought it was packed full of protein goodness.
The best quiche I’ve ever made or eaten anywhere! I added some sautéed onions.
This was good but I added ham to it. I’m going to make it again and try it with sausage.
very good flavor--i add a few simmered tomatillos for a more tangy flavor
This quiche is now a staple in my home. I will typically take a recipe and make changes to my liking but this recipe is perfect, don’t change a thing, delicious.
It turned very delicious with and lovely consistence and wonderful flavor. Definitely making this again.

I have made this quiche multiple times and love it's versatility. I use spinach or kale and add whatever veggies I have including red bell pepper, onion, garlic, asparagus, etc. It always turns out delicious. I also add a few red pepper flakes. Like using the nonfat cottage cheese so that not as much cheese needed.
